frameAlternates.note: The sign-in field of /login (Claude Code 2.1.325, lab 2026-11-15, claude--v2325-login-*.txt): under the rule, `Login`, the sign-in address wrapped at the pane's edge, then `Paste code here if prompted >` and `Esc to cancel`. The field shows each character as `*` but the last six (`***************ESTATE`), and a text longer than the row as `*` cut with `…`, with no space after `>`.

The sign-in field of Claude Code's FIRST RUN, an empty config folder (2.1.325, lab 2026-11-15, claude--v2325-first-run-*.txt): no rule, no `Login` title and no `Esc to cancel` (Esc does nothing there). Under the welcome art's dotted last row (or, below about 50 columns, the `Welcome to Claude Code v…` row, the art is not drawn), the sign-in address from column 0, then ` Paste code here if prompted >` from column 1. The same mask as /login, but a text longer than the row wraps under the label, 31 columns in, and is never cut; only the last row shows clear characters (`wrap`): 21 characters at 40 columns draw `********`, `********`, `STATE`.

idle.dialogRowsNote: Claude Code 2.1.325's first-run theme step (an empty config folder, lab 2026-11-15, claude--v2325-first-run-theme-*): `Let's get started.` over `Choose the text style that looks best with your terminal` and an unnumbered list, no footer, no key named, and Esc does nothing. The theme grammar (harness/claude/first-run-theme.ts) lifts it as a pointed list (a tap walks the pointer with Down or Up and sends Enter, measured live 2026-11-16); this row stays as the wider net, so a screen with these words and no list Collie reads still names a dialog, and the composer never types into it. `/theme` in a session draws the same list under a `Theme` title with `Enter to select · Esc to cancel` and no `Let's get started.`.
idle.signInRowsNote: Claude Code 2.1.325 draws its sign-in field after `Paste code here if prompted >`, on /login two columns in and on the first run one (lab 2026-11-15). The two layouts above read the two shapes and draw the card; this row is the wider net: a screen that ends near such a row and shows no ordinary input box keeps no draft and no line of what is sent there, whatever else is drawn around it.
idle.signInErrorsNote: Claude Code 2.1.325 answers a code it did not take with `OAuth error: That code wasn't accepted…` where the field stood, then `Press Enter to retry.` (lab 2026-11-15, claude--v2325-login-bad-code--w61.txt). A code send that reads it ends refused (`code_rejected`) with those words.
idle.signInSettleMsNote: After a code is submitted Claude Code checks it with its server before it draws `Login successful` or the error (2026-11-16, Altan's run on the dev lane: a good code ended `unknown`, S2's 3 s were not enough). The screen between the two is not captured yet; this bound is a guess on the safe side, and only delays the receipt.

placeholders.textsNote: Claude Code 2.1.328 paints `Resend your message to try again` (a no-break space after the prompt marker) inside the empty box after a turn fails on an API error. It is faint on a styled read; on herdr-core the read is plain text, so only these exact words tell it from a draft (capture 2026-11-19, a refused connection). The text must match whole: the same words with more typed after them stay a draft.
placeholders.patternsNote: Live 2026-10-30, Claude Code 2.1.314 on herdr-core: the empty box rotates faint hints (`Try "refactor <filepath>"`, `Try "fix lint errors"`, `Try "how do I log an error?"`). herdr-core reads the screen as plain text, so the faint attribute is gone and the hint read as a draft; a walky talky delivery stayed held as draft present. The shape counts only on a read with no styling at all; on a styled read the faint attribute decides, so a typed `Try "…"` stays a draft. Fixture surface/claude--v2-1-314-placeholder-plain--w120 (plain text, as herdr-core reads it).
placeholders.anyTextNote: M78 spec 06, 2026-10-30: after a turn the empty box shows a faint prompt suggestion in free words (`cat hello.txt to verify`, `fix it`, `save it to docs/terminal-history.md`). No text, prefix or pattern names it; on herdr-core the faint attribute is gone and the suggestion read as a draft, so a send was refused draft_present. On a read with no styling the Send Protocol proves such a box by its probe: a suggestion is not in the input, so the probe character lands at the start of the box. Fixtures claude--done, claude--ghost-suggestion and the claude-lab--statusline-* set, stripped of SGR.

below.hintsNote: Live check 2026-10-30, Claude Code 2.1.312 over tmux, 120 columns: a fresh pane draws `You've used 75% of your weekly limit · resets Nov 4, 2am (…) · /usage-credits to keep using Claude Code` under the footer, and drops it once the box grows to two rows. The rows under the box went from 2 to 1 and the send ended typed_not_submitted (changed). The pattern covers any percentage and any limit name (`weekly`, `5-hour`, `Opus weekly`); the tail after `limit` is free. Fixture claude--v2312-weekly-limit-row--w120. Lab 2026-11-01, Claude Code 2.1.316 over tmux (focus-events off, the tmux default), 100 columns: while a turn runs, Claude draws `tmux focus-events off · add 'set -g focus-events on' to ~/.tmux.conf and reattach for focus tracking` under the footer, and drops it once the box holds a draft of two paragraphs (the footer turns to `ctrl+g to edit in nano`). The rows under the box went from 2 to 1 and a two-paragraph send into the turn ended typed_not_submitted (changed); the same send with focus-events on, on an idle box, and over Herdr was sent. Fixtures bridge/surface/fixtures/claude--v2316-two-paragraphs-*--w100. Remote Control (2.1.319, issue 767, a field report, not a capture): Claude draws `/rc`, `/rc active`, `/rc connecting…`, `/rc reconnecting` or `/rc failed` as a row of its own under the footer and may draw or drop it while Collie types; the pattern matches that whole row and nothing longer, so the focused `/rc · enter to view` and a pointed `❯ /rc` still count. Fixture claude--v2319-rc-footer-idle--w100 (built). Live check 2026-11-13, Claude Code 2.1.323 over tmux, 100 columns, `claude --remote-control`: the pill is right-aligned in the footer, `/rc active` (`/rc` after five sightings), and shares the mode row when it fits or takes a row of its own under a full-width notice, so the rows under the box move between one and three on their own; the pattern is right for the own-row form, spaces and all. Dialogs draw no footer, so no pill stands under one. Fixtures claude--v2323-rc-on-*.
below.footerRowsNote: Field case 2026-11-13, Claude Code 2.1.323 over Herdr, lane 8788: a send went into a running turn while the session resumed a background agent (SendMessage, 17:38:02.055Z, inside the 2.5 s S1 window that began at about 17:38:02.0Z). The agents panel under the box gained a `◯` row, the rows under the box no longer matched S0's count, and the send ended typed_not_submitted (changed) with the text in the box. The panel's rows (`chrome: true`) add, drop and redraw on their own while the box keeps the keys, so the Send Protocol leaves them out of its count, but only inside a panel the frame walk accepted: a blank row over `● main`, then only panel rows to the bottom. The mode row's `↓ to view` hint (tasks-view-hint) is no chrome. Repro bridge/surface/protocol.test.ts, "the agents panel under the box is chrome".

paste.imageNote: Lab 2026-10-21, Claude Code 2.1.305 over herdr: a whole-text paste loses each piece (cut at a newline, and at a space before an absolute path) that is an existing .png/.jpg/.jpeg/.gif/.webp file at an absolute path, any case; each shows as `[Image #N]` before the rest, and the kept pieces are joined by newlines. A missing file, a .txt, a file without extension, a `~/` or a relative path, and a path with words after it stay text. Lab 2026-10-30, Claude Code 2.1.312 over tmux: the path is attached only when it is the WHOLE paste (`[Image #1]`); a path among other text stays text, cut onto a row of its own after the space, and a fold counts every typed line break (42 lines with a path: `+41 lines`; one 900-character line with the path: `[Pasted text #1]`). The compare takes both forms (`WholePaste.literal`), after the field case of 2026-10-29 where a two-paragraph message with the path was typed and never submitted.
paste.blockNote: Lab 2026-10-20, Claude Code 2.1.304 over herdr: one bracketed paste of the whole text folds to `[Pasted text #N +M lines]`, M the line breaks (60 lines: +59; 30 short lines: +29); 3 short lines land literally; a 700-word line folds to `[Pasted text #N]`.
